accepted_licences_reason: The daily release job's accepted list (LICENCES in daily_library_release.sh); a compound expression is accepted when every identifier in it is on this list and it uses no WITH exception.
near_duplicate_reason: Measured on the 8,847 stored supply components on September 28, 2026: at 9/10, 175 API operation packages were flagged, every inspected pair a distinct operation of one template (different method or path), with the highest similarity 0.964. Text similarity at 49/50 therefore only catches copies that differ in a few words; the job key below catches two packages for one job whatever their text.

minified_code.literal_statement_reason: A Python line longer than the limit is exempt when it holds exactly one statement that only displays literal data (names, constants, and dict, list, tuple or set displays), such as a generated operation's keyword dictionary: on September 28, 2026, ten AWS operation modules carried such lines of 1,282 to 1,562 characters. A JavaScript line is exempt when it holds exactly one constant declaration whose whole value parses as JSON, such as a generated client's parameter table or a test's example body: the September 30 run refused 7,539 API operation packages for such lines alone. Several statements on one line, the mark of minified code, are never exempt.

metadata_fact_reason: A registry entry, package metadata or repository facts record is read for names, versions, package identifiers and counts only; no text of it is copied into the package (the MCP line's link mode, basis link_only_facts_no_text_copied; the program line's GitHub repository facts). Such a fact may carry NOASSERTION when none of its bytes is a package file and at least one governing fact (licence text, specification, data, formula) carries an accepted licence. Terms of use (an API's terms of service, a site's licence page) are read for the clauses that permit the read and state the assets' licence, pinned by digest so a reviewer can read them again; they grant no licence to any byte and none of their text is copied, so they carry NOASSERTION like the other metadata (the creative line's Poly Haven and ambientCG terms, October 5, 2026).
effect_text_reason: The licensed import's effect rules read words as actions a harness is told to take, which is right for instruction, skill, command and configuration files. A README, a JSON Schema or code comments of a generated client describe a remote API ('uploads a file'), whose effect the network effect covers; on September 28, 2026 those words produced 501 false effect findings (reads_files and writes_files in README.md and schema.json) on components whose syntax trees touch no local file. Python code is judged by its syntax tree.
job_key_reason: One package for one job: an API operation is its specification file and its operation (method, path and the specification's operation identifier, since a specification may define several operations on one method and path, as Box does with URL fragments and OpenAI with beta variants: 23 such packages were refused as copies on September 28, 2026 when the key held method and path only); a protocol server is its registry package; a program is its formula; a data table or a copied schema is its upstream file bytes, not counting licence texts and notice files, which every package of one source shares; a schema generated from an API specification copies no upstream file, so it is its specification and its title (the September 30 run refused 8,787 of 9,142 schema packages as one job because the key held only the notice files or nothing). An animation scene is where its documentation shows it (the documented module, class or page) and its scene name, with its occurrence when one location shows two scenes of one name (Arrow's docstring shows two different ArrowExample scenes in Manim Community v0.21.0), and never the release tag, so the same scene read at two releases is one job. A publisher's table is its publisher and its series (schema.json x-baltor-table), never its bytes, its archive member's name or its retrieval time: a World Bank series retrieved twice, its values revised in between, is one job, and two series are two (publisher_tables, October 5, 2026). Two components with one job key are duplicates whatever their text. An API tool server is its specification file: the repository and path its server module declares, and the specification's address without its commit, so two revisions of one file are one job and two files are two, whatever tools each holds. A creative asset recipe or editable project is its source and its asset or project identity (job.source and job.identity of creative.json), never its commit, resolution or format: the resolutions and formats of one asset are variants inside one package, so two packages pinning other resolutions of one asset, or one demo project at two commits, are one job.
asset_role_reason: A reference or creative form (catalogue_attributes.ASSET_ROLE_FORMS: an image, a mask, a pose layout, a 3D or CAD model, a template, a code example) is bytes a harness interprets, so it is served with the asset role that says what the harness does with them (reference, generation input, editable source, test evidence), and the release bundle refuses such a form without one. A line that writes these forms names the package file and the field that state the role (the creative line: asset.asset_role of creative.json, October 9, 2026); the manifest check refuses a package of that line whose role is missing or outside the vocabulary, and admission serves the stated role as the item's asset_role attribute.

composition.targets_reason: Builder e's library_composition_targets/v1 (September 27, 2026) is the authority once integrated; these shares are its copy for a checkout that does not hold it yet.

licence_fingerprint_reason: Each licence text a package carries must be recognized as a licence on the accepted list, and together the texts must grant every identifier of the declared expression. Measured on a random 2,500 of the stored supply on September 28, 2026: every text was recognized except one Unlicense text, which the accepted list already refuses.
documented_fields_reason: A generated client's README names the operation it calls (METHOD /path); code whose operation differs from its description is refused. Measured on 1,427 stored API operation packages on September 28, 2026: every README named its operation. A generated tool server's README names the repository of the specification its tool table was written from.

mutation.replacement: raise RuntimeError('qualification mutant: this implementation was replaced')
mutation.reason: The written criteria require verification that rejects a known-wrong result. Every public function and public method of each root module is replaced by one that raises, and the package's own tests must then fail. On September 28, 2026 the Tactical reviewer approved every planted package whose code was broken in ways its tests could not see; this check needs no reviewer.
mutation.javascript_replacement: throw new Error('qualification mutant: this implementation was replaced');

download_reason: A download is pinned by its SHA-256; the digest guarantees the bytes whatever the transport, as Homebrew itself accepts for source archives. Measured on September 28, 2026: the figlet recipe's source archive is served over ftp with its SHA-256 and was refused while the rule required https. A line that pins downloads in another file names it as its download_manifest (the creative line's creative.json); every address there is checked the same way.
address_reason: A fact source or an upstream copy is pinned by an https address and its SHA-256; a download may use another transport because its digest is checked where it is installed.
tested_code_reason: The sandbox runs Python modules and their unittest tests, and the mutation check rewrites Python. A package holding code in another language is refused until its runner and mutation are declared here, so that implementation_tested never covers code nothing ran. Builder e announced JavaScript clients for the API line on September 28, 2026; node 22 is installed at /usr/bin/node for the runner. On October 9, 2026 the sandbox gained a JavaScript runner: root test_*.mjs files run with node --test (TAP reporter) under the same namespaces and limits, and the mutation check replaces every export of a root .mjs module with one that throws. Plain .js and .cjs files still have no declared runner and stay refused.
environment_reason: A run that timed out or could not start its sandbox says nothing about the component: on September 28, 2026, 12 of 23,523 components timed out while the machine's load average was near 300 and passed when run again. Such a component stays refused in that run (it is never admitted untested) and its record is never reused, so the next run checks it again.
